a.notes: Year: 1996 is the museum itself. Its predecessor, the Halle für internationale neue Kunst (InK), is dated 1977 (one source) or summer 1978 (Migros corporate timeline) and closed in 1981; it is not counted here. One Zürich tourism page says 'since 1966', which conflicts with the other dates and looks like a typo, so it was ignored. The 1996 statement is attributed to a tourism page and the Migros corporate timeline, not the museum's own site. Address: the sources are tourism and listing pages, not the museum's own site. One listing gives postcode 8005, while the others consistently give 8031. A listing also gives a separate mailing address, Postfach 1766, 8031 Zürich.

b.year_basis: founded (museum established 1996; the Migros collection itself dates from the 1950s)

b.address_statement: The visitor address is Limmatstrasse 270, 8005 Zurich, and the postal address is P.O. Box 1766, 8031 Zurich.
b.notes: Postcode: third-party listings gave 8031 or 8005; the museum's own contact page gives 8005 for the visitor address and 8031 only for the postal address (P.O. Box 1766), so 8005 is used. The year sentences came in a search summary that cites the museum's own About page and the Migros corporate timeline; I could not separate which of the two URLs carries each sentence word for word, so both are listed. Other dates in the results that are not the founding of the museum: Migros collection begun in the late 1950s by Gottlieb Duttweiler; Migros 'Halle für Internationale neue Kunst' exhibition hall 1978-1981; reopened 31 August 2012 after renovation (2010-2012).

b.address_statement: The phone number is +44 (0)1865 722733, the general email is info@modernartoxford.org.uk, and the address is 30 Pembroke Street, Oxford OX1 1BP.

Same body: called Museum of Modern Art, Oxford until 2002, then renamed Modern Art Oxford. Opening hours differ between the site's pages but this does not affect the values.

a.year_basis: founded (donation contract between Peter and Irene Ludwig and the City of Cologne)
a.year_statement: On February 23, 1976 Peter and Irene Ludwig and the City of Cologne signed a donation contract founding the Museum Ludwig.
a.address_statement: The museum is at Heinrich-Böll-Platz, 50667 Cologne, directly beside Cologne Cathedral, across from Cologne Central Station.
a.notes: Year: the official history gives the founding as 1976. The exact day differs between versions of the official page (23 February and 5 February), but the year is the same. The building opened in 1986 and is not used as the year. The collection also traces back to Josef Haubrich's 1946 donation to the city, which is not the founding of this museum. The museum shared its building with the Wallraf-Richartz Museum until 1994, when it was decided to separate them. Address: the source gives no house number. One listing (In Your Pocket) gives Bischofsgartenstraße 1, which the results suggest is the Gesellschaft für Moderne Kunst office address or the accessible entrance, not the main venue address, so it was not used.

b.year_basis: founded (donation contract signed by Peter and Irene Ludwig and the City of Cologne; the museum building opened in 1986)
b.year_statement: The Museum Ludwig was founded in 1976 through a donation from Peter and Irene Ludwig.
b.address_statement: The Museum Ludwig is at Heinrich-Böll-Platz, 50667 Cologne.
b.notes: The results say the official history page gives the signing date as 23 February 1976 and an older version of the page gives 5 February 1976; both are 1976, so the year is unaffected. Not the founding year: the current building opened in 1986 as a shared 'double museum' with the Wallraf-Richartz Museum, and the two institutions were split in 1994; Josef Haubrich's 1946 gift of his Expressionist collection to the city is described as the collection's earlier core. The results give no house number for the address, and the history page refers to the building as being on Bischofsgartenstrasse; the address is given as the official site writes it.

Address: Sortiraparis gives 60 rue des Archives, but the Ministry of Culture register and most sources give 62. The search tool returned synthesized summaries, so the sentences quoted are from those summaries. The URL for the year is the museum's own page; the URL for the address is the Ministry register.

b.year_basis: inaugurated / opened as a museum (21 February 1967); the official site also says the museum was founded in 1967
b.year_statement: The chassenature.org page says the museum was inaugurated by André Malraux in the Hôtel de Guénégaud, a 17th-century building by François Mansart, on February 21, 1967, and was extended in 2007 to the adjacent Hôtel de Mongelas.
b.address_statement: Most sources give 62 rue des Archives, 75003 Paris, in the Marais.
b.notes: Year conflict explained by two events: the search results say most sources credit the Sommers with founding it in 1964 (offi.fr, per the result text, ties 1964 to the foundation the Sommers set up), while the official chassenature.org page gives the inauguration as 21 Feb 1967 and says the museum was founded in 1967. 1967 is used because it is the official site's date and the public opening. The result text did not attribute the sentence to one link, so the URLs listed are the Links entries whose results the summary drew on. Check against the official site.
